description:
FILED s543q (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28, CODE 6a1301ed = MAIN-READY-114 + records, v2-16500) by the Rosetta census B (docs/rosetta-plan.md section 6b; #2104).

THE SHAPES (neutral reproducers, run on the tree, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL; perl prints 123 for each):

    do { last if $_ > 3; print $_ } for 1 .. 1e10;              PCL: dies (below)
    my $big = 1e10; do { last if $_ > 3; print $_ } for 1 .. $big;   PCL: dies
    do { last if $_ > 3; print $_ } for 1 .. 10_000_000_000;    PCL: dies
    use constant BIG => 1e10;
    for my $i (1 .. BIG) { last if $i > 3; print $i }           PCL: dies (also with BIG => 10_000_000_000)
    for my $i (1 .. 1e10) { last if $i > 3; print $i }          PCL: 123 (right)
    my $big = 1e10; for my $i (1 .. $big) { ... }               PCL: 123 (right)

    the death: "Unhandled simple-error ... Out of memory during list extend" + a Lisp backtrace, exit 1 (perl's message for a
    range that IS materialized, `my @a = (1 .. 1e10)`, raised with a bare CL `error`: #1427's census)

WHERE (emitted Lisp): the modifier form is `(p-foreach ($_ (p-.. 1 1.0d10)) ...)` and the constant-end block form
`(p-foreach-raw ($i (p-.. 1 1.0d10)) :my t ...)` -- p-.. builds the list (its size check raises at 1e8 elements); the block
form with a literal or a variable end gets the counting loop (`p-foreach-range`, #61).  So the counting-loop choice is made
before the constant is folded, and the modifier form never makes it.  Below 1e8 the same shapes RUN but build the whole list
first (a speed and memory cost on every `... for 1 .. $n` statement; not measured here).

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (taken): 0557 and 1291 with the loop written in the block form over a VARIABLE end
(`my $inf = Inf; for ($start .. $inf) { ... }`) are byte-identical to perl -- the only cause of both.

PROGRAMS: 0557-Gapful-numbers, 1291-Smallest-square-that-begins-with-n.
frequency_reason: Rosetta: 0557-Gapful-numbers (`$g .= do { ... last } for $start .. Inf`), 1291-Smallest-square-that-begins-with-n (`do { ... last if ... } for 1..Inf`), both with `use constant Inf => 1e10` / `10e12`
subject: LOUD / UNTIDY: a foreach over a RANGE is MATERIALIZED as a list in two spellings -- the statement MODIFIER `EXPR for A .. B` (any endpoints) and the block form whose end is a `use constant` (`for my $i (1 .. BIG)`) -- so the `for 1 .. Inf` + `last` idiom dies "Out of memory during list extend" with a raw Lisp backtrace; perl's foreach range is a counter (Rosetta 0557 1291)
triage_reason: a foreach over a range never builds its list in perl (perlop "Range Operators": "in the current implementation, no temporary array is created when the range operator is used as the expression in foreach loops"), IN by docs/supported-subset.md section 3
